answer: Name: shared-cost identity thread. Each new identity must join a coordination thread whose members jointly pay a per-period operating charge regardless of activity, which a kernel contract enforces by splitting the bill evenly across active members. Idle or duplicate identities still owe their share, so a sybil set of n agents costs n times the base fee even if it never transacts. Membership is capped per thread and audited on a public terrace of period totals, making mass registration visibly expensive. Attackers pay continuous rent, not a one-time fee.
